note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  1-week history of sore throat → dry, non-productive cough with mild exertional shortness of breath, occasional wheeze, chest discomfort; subjective low-grade fever first 3 days; intermittent headaches; reduced appetite; no known chronic diseases or risk factors documented.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother—lung cancer; no other family history recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  None routinely; advised paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Exercises “now and then”; non-smoker (experimented once or twice); no alcohol or other substance use mentioned; recent appetite loss.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Expressed health-related anxiety about cough; no formal mood assessment recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Working adult; required 2 days sick leave this week; lives in UK; no housing or financial issues documented.  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Acute onset sore throat progressing to dry cough; mild exertional dyspnoea and wheeze; brief low-grade fever; no sputum or haemoptysis; mother with lung cancer; non-smoker; no significant comorbidities. Examination and investigations not performed (telehealth).

Working diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory infection / viral bronchitis—high likelihood based on typical symptom sequence and improving trend.

Supporting differentials (consistent with DDx):
• COVID-19 infection – medium likelihood; similar symptom cluster (sore throat, dry cough, fever, appetite loss); recommend testing if symptoms persist or worsen.  
• Reactive airway disease / new-onset asthma – medium likelihood; presence of wheeze and exertional SOB may indicate airway hyper-reactivity, possibly triggered by viral illness.

Management:
• Symptomatic treatment: paracetamol, adequate fluids, rest.  
• Issued sick note for additional work leave.  
• Safety-net advice: seek in-person medical review if breathlessness worsens, new chest pain, persistent fever, or no improvement within 4–5 days.  
• Consider COVID testing if clinically indicated.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Advised fluids, rest, and symptom monitoring; no broader preventive counselling documented.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Reassurance and symptom relief; obtain sick note.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  None at this stage; advised to see GP if deterioration.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Not recorded (verbal advice only).  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  specialist_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  dental_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  optometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  audiometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  social_support_referral_or_not_recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection / viral bronchitis – High likelihood: classic 1-week progression of sore throat to dry cough, low-grade fever, fluctuating recovery, no alarming features.  
2. COVID-19 infection – Medium likelihood: matching symptom constellation (sore throat, dry cough, fever, headache, appetite loss); testing status unknown.  
3. Reactive airway disease / new-onset asthma – Medium likelihood: wheeze and exertional SOB suggest airway hyper-reactivity triggered by current illness.

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, physical exam findings, BMI, immunisation review, chronic disease screening, formal follow-up plan.  
● Internal conflicts: Recorded DOB (9 May 2016) inconsistent with adult history—conflict noted.
